results.text:
Australians missing in the Nepal floods: what we know so far

The number of Australians missing in the Nepal-Tibet flash flooding disaster has fallen from 36 to 35, after another person was confirmed safe on Tuesday. The Australian citizen, who was in Nepal and uncontactable in the wake of the flash flooding on 26 August, confirmed they were safe and well and did not require consular assistance. It comes after seven previously unaccounted for Australians were confirmed safe in recent days, with one found in Nepal, one in Tibet and three outside the crisis-hit area. A Sydney woman, Cara Severino, 25, was also safely located in Nepal more than two days after the floods. The names of the Australians confirmed safe have not yet been released. Pilgrims trekking to a holy site in Tibet make up the majority of Australians who have been reported missing after the deadly flash floods and landslides tore through valleys on the Nepal-Tibet border. Most were travelling with Himalayan Glacier Adventures, Kailash Journeys and the Isha Foundation. Related: ‘The house got carried 100 metres away’: some Nepal flood victims had minutes of notice.

citation.title: Australians missing in the Nepal floods: what we know so far

results.text:
Number of Australians missing in Nepal’s deadly floods rises again, as Albanese deploys more personnel

The number of Australians who were reported missing in the catastrophic Nepal flooding disaster has risen to 41, as one family celebrates after an unaccounted-for woman made contact with them yesterday. It means three additional Australians were confirmed missing overnight – up from 38 who remained unaccounted for on Friday evening. The Australian government’s Department of Foreign Affairs has been urgently working with local authorities to contact Australian woman Cara Severino, 25, who became the first Australian reported missing who has been confirmed safe. Related: ‘So desperately loved’: ADF member among dozens of Australians missing in Nepal floods as families pray for safe return Severino contacted her parents, Debbie and Frank Severino, on Friday morning, informing them she was hiking away from the disaster zone to Kathmandu with a group of Nepali hikers – a trek of more than 110km.
